reason: I re-checked this at 16:04Z and the diagnosis holds. The Kernel-Power events show the laptop entering Modern Standby at 14:59:00Z (Reason: Lid). The power source changed at 14:59:01Z. The network dropped at 14:59:11Z (172 Disconnected, Adaptive Connected Standby). There was a brief wake at 15:15:31Z, and the laptop went back into standby because the battery drain budget was exceeded; the network dropped again at 15:15:42Z (Policy Setting). It came out of standby at 15:39:48Z (Lid). In poll.log, the gap from 14:54:21Z to 15:41:53Z, with the NameResolutionError at 15:15:31Z, lines up exactly with these events. So the CONTEXT entry of 15:43Z ('network outage, not a sleep') is wrong. The situation is more urgent than the finding says. The laptop is still on battery (BatteryStatus 1) and was at 58% at 16:04Z. It was 64% at 15:49Z, so it is draining at about 24% an hour and will be empty around 18:30Z (21:30 MSK). That is before probe 51 is read (21:30-22:15Z) and before the freeze and night-batch crons. I found three flaws in the proposed action. (a) The keep-awake process (SetThreadExecutionState) does not stop lid-close standby; it only prevents idle standby. (b) The command 'setacvalueindex LIDACTION 0' only applies on AC; on battery, closing the lid still puts the laptop to sleep. So the charger is the main thing to ask for, and the lid setting is a backup. (c) Everything runs until the finals tick at 29 Sep 20:00Z (23:00 MSK), and so does the poller (W6), so the charger and keep-awake must last until then, not 15:00 MSK or 12:00Z. A single battery check at 23:25Z also comes too late, because the battery may already be dead. No model value is involved, so rules R1-R10 do not apply. This is operations only, and it is cheap and reversible.
fix: Send one Russian message to the user now (MSK first). Tell him the 18:05-18:35 MSK outage was the laptop going to sleep on battery with the lid closed. The battery is now at 58% and draining at about 24% an hour, so it will be empty around 21:30 MSK, before the probe 51 read. Ask him to plug in the charger now and leave it in until 23:00 MSK 29 Sep. Ask him to keep the lid open. Optionally, he can run these commands himself (all reversible): powercfg /setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_BUTTONS LIDACTION 0 ; powercfg /change monitor-timeout-ac 0 ; powercfg /setactive SCHEME_CURRENT. Tell him the lid setting only works while the charger is plugged in. Only if he says yes: start a detached keep-awake process (ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED) that runs until 29 Sep 20:00Z. Note that it does not stop sleep when the lid is closed. Correct the CONTEXT entry of 15:43Z to 'Modern Standby on battery (lid), not DNS'. Replace the single 23:25Z check with a check every 30 minutes starting now, through 29 Sep 20:00Z. Send a push notification when BatteryStatus is not 2 and charge is below 40%, or when a poll.log header is more than 15 minutes old. At 23:25Z, check once more that BatteryStatus is 2 before the freeze.
realistic_gain: No LB gain; this protects the schedule. Without the charger, the laptop is likely to die around 18:30Z. That would lose the probe 51 read, the 00:05Z/00:06Z/00:46Z night slots, the freeze and night-batch crons, and every morning decision on the 29 Sep table that depends on them. The cost is one message and the user plugging in the charger.
